rows.jp: 「いや、姉弟喧嘩なんてごくまっとうな人生じゃん。止めんよ」
rows.en: “Sibling fights are a perfectly normal part of life. I’m not getting in the way.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."
ghs.assessment: 止めんよ means the speaker will not interfere with or stop the siblings' quarrel. 'Don'tcha stop' changes the first-person decision into an imperative telling Tomoki to continue.
ghs.remedy: Use 'No. A sibling quarrel is a perfectly normal part of life. I won't interfere.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."

ghs.en: Tomoki: "..."

rows.jp: 「要するに俺様を手伝えということだ」
rows.en: “Bottom line: your job is to help yours truly.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."
ghs.assessment: 'The greatness that is I' uses the wrong pronoun case and awkwardly expands 俺様.
ghs.remedy: Use 'In short, you're here to help the great me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."

rows.en: I puffed out my chest.

ghs.en: Puff that chest with pride!
ghs.assessment: A stage-direction or imperative reading is possible from the Japanese fragment. The English is presentation-ambiguous rather than a critical wrong-subject reversal.
ghs.remedy: Present the action with a clear actor.

highlights.text: Puff that chest with pride!

rows.en: “...You’re a piece of work.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."
ghs.assessment: おまえ大物 is an impressed or incredulous judgment that the addressee is really something. 'What're you a VIP' is not grammatical and treats 大物 as a literal status question.
ghs.remedy: Use '...You really are something.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."

rows.jp: 「適応係数８０オーバーのオーバーロードですから」
rows.en: “My adaptation coefficient is over eighty. That makes me an Overlord.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."
ghs.assessment: The source says the speaker is an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient above eighty. The English makes him ruler 'of all those' above eighty, adding a hierarchy and other people.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient over eighty.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."

rows.jp: 「……そのオーバーロードとも、これからも普通に友達してやるよ」
rows.en: “...Overlord or not, I’ll still be your friend. Same as always.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...and I will still be this Overlord's normal friend from now on."
ghs.assessment: The source promises to keep treating even this self-styled Overlord as an ordinary friend. 'This Overlord's normal friend' turns 'ordinary' into a property of the friend and muddles the continuing relationship.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Even with an Overlord like that, I'll go on being your friend like normal.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...and I will still be this Overlord's normal friend from now on."

rows.jp: 「そういうの、嫌いじゃないから」
rows.en: “I don’t dislike that about you.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."
ghs.assessment: そういうの refers to that kind of behavior or attitude. 'That of you' is ungrammatical and changes the demonstrative into a property possessed by the addressee.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I don't dislike that kind of thing.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."

rows.jp: さっと校舎内に消えた。逃げるように。
rows.en: He ducked into the school like he was running away.

ghs.en: He quickly vanishes inside the school building. As if running away.

rows.en: “‘I DON’T DISLIKE THAT ABOUT YOU’... Pff!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Iiii don't haaate that of youuu'... pffft!"
ghs.assessment: The line mockingly repeats the immediately preceding sentiment. 'That of you' remains ungrammatical even inside the imitation and obscures the exact callback.
ghs.remedy: Mock the established English line while preserving its wording, for example 'I don't disliiike that kind of thiiing...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "'Iiii don't haaate that of youuu'... pffft!"

rows.jp: そう言った友貴は、一瞬で人類の限界まで赤面しきっていた。
rows.en: When he said it, Tomoki had gone red enough to test the limits of the human species.

ghs.en: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.
ghs.assessment: 'Reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind' is an over-literal and syntactically congested rendering of the hyperbole that he blushed to the human limit.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tomoki had instantly turned as red as humanly possible.'

highlights.text: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.

rows.jp: 「照れるくらいなら言うんじゃねーっての。まったく」
rows.en: “If saying it embarrasses you that much, then don’t say it. Honestly.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If it makes you embarrassed then don'tcha say it! Seriously."

rows.en: I looked up at the antenna.

ghs.en: I look up at the antenna.

rows.jp: 「でも、これでちっとは進捗すんな」
rows.en: “Still, this should move things along a little.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But with this, we're a little on the way aren't we."
ghs.assessment: Progress remains identifiable through unidiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Render the progress statement naturally.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But with this, we're a little on the way aren't we."

rows.en: Our happy little pretend club.

ghs.en: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.
ghs.assessment: The pretend-club proposition survives. The confirmed defects are grammar and idiom.
ghs.remedy: Use grammatical English preserving the pretense.

highlights.text: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.

rows.jp: 大切な思い出となりえる。
rows.en: It might become a treasured memory—

ghs.en: They may become precious memories.
ghs.assessment: The plural club-activity antecedent is contextually available. The remaining defect is unidiomatic recollection grammar.
ghs.remedy: Refer naturally to the remembered club activities.

highlights.text: They may become precious memories.

rows.jp: いつか、楽しい夢を見るための―――%Nきっと。
rows.en: one that would let me dream a happy dream someday—%Nsurely.

ghs.en: For the sake of one day having that fun dream---

rows.en: Forever.

ghs.en: Forever.

rows.jp: ありがとうと、思うため。
rows.en: So that I could feel grateful.

ghs.en: For the sake of thinking... thank you.
ghs.assessment: The source expresses the purpose of someday being able to think or say 'thank you.' 'For the sake of thinking... thank you' does not form a grammatical English relation between purpose and quoted thought.
ghs.remedy: Use 'So that I can think: thank you.'

highlights.text: For the sake of thinking... thank you.

rows.jp: 俺は戦っているんだと思う。
rows.en: I think that’s what I’m fighting for.

ghs.en: I will be fighting.
ghs.assessment: 俺は戦っているんだと思う is a present reflective claim: 'I think this is what I'm fighting for.' The English changes it to future tense and omits the governing 'I think.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I think that is what I am fighting for.'

highlights.text: I will be fighting.
